setup_cmds: python -m pip install -q yfinance mftool tenacity pdfplumber

tasks.spec: Per phase brief 'services/market_data.py'. get_current_price(symbol,asset_type) branched by asset type (NOT linear chain); _fetch_yfinance/_fetch_mftool with tenacity(3 attempts, wait_exponential 2..10s); normalize_symbol adds .NS/.BO for Indian equity/ETF; batch_refresh(holdings,total_retry_budget_s=120) with a shared budget; bond/other -> return None + caller excludes from value. get_last_cached_price reads the latest_prices view via services.db.connect().
Port Screens/Finance/Calculations/compute_the_xirr.py: xirr(cashflows: list[(date, amount)]) -> float via Newton/bisection fallback. Pure function, no I/O.

Per phase brief 'services/calculations/backfill.py'. backfill_price_history(symbol,asset_type): stock/etf -> yfinance history period='2y'; mutual_fund -> mftool NAV history by resolved AMFI scheme code; else return. bulk INSERT OR IGNORE into price_history via services.db. Also a tiny module-level queue: enqueue_backfill(symbol,asset_type) + run_pending() a BackgroundTasks callable uses, so imports never block.

Per phase brief 'services/calculations/holdings_upsert.py'. upsert_holding(account_id,symbol,name,type_,new_units,new_cost_per_unit,currency,source,purchase_date,mode). mode='add_lot': weighted-average-cost merge (master doc section 10) + idempotent lot insert (catch UNIQUE violation, pass). mode='set_snapshot': SET units to new_units, do not add. new_cost_per_unit is None -> keep existing avg_cost, skip recompute. On first-ever symbol import call backfill.enqueue_backfill (not inline).

Port CAS PDF parsing from Screens/Finance/Calculations/pull_from_cas_statement.py: open with PAN password (os.environ['CAS_PAN'] or from backend/.env), extract fund rows + resolve AMFI scheme code, snapshot semantics (total units held). parse_cas(file_bytes) -> list[dict] normalized rows. No CSV file writes.
parse_groww_csv(file_bytes) -> list[dict] rows (symbol,name,units,cost_per_unit,purchase_date,source='groww'). Tolerant of Groww's holdings-export column names.

dedupe_transaction(conn, account_id, date, amount, description) -> bool (True if new, inserts; False if a row with the same normalized date+amount+description exists). parse_upi_csv(file_bytes) and parse_sms(text) both return normalized txn dicts and BOTH persist via dedupe_transaction â€” one code path, no double counting.

APIRouter. GET/POST /accounts (POST body: name,type,institution?,currency?). GET/PUT/DELETE /accounts/{id} â€” DELETE returns 409 with a message pointing to archive when ON DELETE RESTRICT trips. POST /accounts/{id}/archive sets archived_at. List excludes archived unless ?include_archived=true. Uses services.db.connect().

APIRouter with CRUD for goals, insurance, salary, debts, holdings mirroring master doc section 7 (goals: store start_date at creation; salary POST always inserts a new row; holdings {id} DELETE only if zero lots else 409; {id}/archive). All via services.db.connect(), archived filtering as in accounts.

APIRouter: POST /import/manual {entity, ...fields} dispatch to the right table; POST /import/groww-csv (multipart file) -> parse_groww_csv -> upsert_holding(mode='add_lot'); POST /import/cas (multipart pdf) -> parse_cas -> upsert_holding(mode='set_snapshot'); POST /import/upi-csv (multipart) and POST /import/sms {text} -> services.imports.transactions. 10MB upload cap, validate content type before parsing. Schedule backfill.run_pending via BackgroundTasks.

sanitize_for_cloud_llm(payload: dict) -> dict: recursively drop keys/values that are account numbers, PAN, transaction descriptions, account/holding names, lender names, ticker symbols; keep only aggregates (allocation_pct, category_sums, debt_totals_by_type). Supervisor class holds the cloud + local llm clients and INJECTS a client into each specialist it constructs. build_cloud_prompt works from allocation percentages only.

InvestmentSpecialist, DebtSpecialist, TrackerSpecialist, LearningSpecialist â€” each __init__(self, llm_client, calc_services). NO module-level 'import openai'/'ollama'/'litellm'. Each exposes analyze() returning a deterministic dict; the llm_client is used only to render a narrative string field.
